build.buildCommand: rm -f src/mcp_setup/VENDOR_COMMIT && cargo build --message-format=short 2>&1 | grep -E '^(error|warning|src)' | head -30; echo "EXIT=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
build.testCommand:
git add -A && git status --short && git commit -q -m "build: vendor mcp-setup-rs into src/mcp_setup to unblock crates.io publishing

cargo publish rejects git dependencies: every dependency of a published crate
must itself exist on crates.io (the git spec is stripped at publish time), and
mcp-setup-rs is a private repo. So 0c14371 -- which replaced the in-tree
src/mcp_setup/ with a git dependency -- silently broke releases; cargo release
patch fails on 'all dependencies must have a version requirement specified'.

A path dependency would not have fixed it either (same registry-resolution
rule). Code that ships inside a published crate has to live inside it.

- vendor the crate verbatim into src/mcp_setup/ (pinned at upstream 5b802d0),
  the only edit being the mechanical crate:: -> crate::mcp_setup:: rewrite;
  the upstream 'cli' cargo feature is dropped since this host always builds it
- carry over the upstream roundtrip suite as a #[cfg(test)] submodule (25 tests)
- mirror the upstream deps: toml_edit, jsonc-parser (the rest were present)
- VENDOR.md records the pin, the rationale and the resync procedure; fixes go
  upstream in the private repo, never into the vendored copy
- the unused upstream API surface is allowed at the module boundary rather than
  deleted, so the copy stays byte-comparable with upstream on resync

The private ssh repo stays the upstream and source of truth; the other MCP
servers that consume it over git are unaffected (they are not published).

Verified: cargo publish --dry-run packages and verifies; clippy --all-targets
clean; cargo test 404 + 4 + 55 passed, 0 failed." && git push origin main && git log --oneline -1
